_about: Public-domain Seth Williston (1770-1851), Congregational missionary and pastor in western New York and Hopkinsian theologian, for the Word Hoard: Sermons on Doctrinal and Experimental Subjects, A Vindication of some of the most Essential Doctrines of the Reformation, The Harmony of Divine Truth, Christ's Kingdom not of this World, Slavery not a Scriptural Ground of Division, and Five Discourses on the Sabbath. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 105 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

williston-sermons: Sermons, on doctrinal and experimental subjects (Hudson [N.Y.]: Printed by A. Stoddard, no. 137, Warren-street, 1812)
williston-vindication: A vindication of some of the most essential doctrines of the reformation: being a reply to objections raised against these doctrines in a late publication, entitled: "The errors of Hopkinsianism detected and refuted; in six letters, by Nathan Bangs ..." addressed to the author of the present work (Hudson, N.Y., Printed by Ashbel Stoddard, 1817)
williston-harmony: The harmony of divine truth (Utica, N.Y. : Bennett and Bright (for the author), 1836)
williston-christs-kingdom: Christ's kingdom not of this world. The spiritual character of the kingdom of Christ, in three discourses (New York, Saxton & Miles, 1842)
williston-slavery: Slavery not a scriptural ground of division in efforts for the salvation of the heathen (New-York, M.W. Dodd, 1844)
williston-sabbath: Five discourses on the Sabbath : preached at Durham, N.Y (New Haven : Hooker, 1847)

_excluded.williston-columbian: The Columbian Preacher (sermons by several preachers)
_excluded.williston-bangs: The Errors of Hopkinsianism (Nathan Bangs's letters against him)
